papers.text: A motorway bench, where the hedge is, to watch coaches go by. They mostly do.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An extra hour on show day, from the National Clock. Spotters can spare one.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Lampshades for the street lamps. Then tassels. The bus stop's gets both.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Give us the League's telephone. We only ring for early coaches. Twice a year.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Tune one foghorn to the band. Then all of them. Then book a fog.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: We booked the bandstand on the band's form. Instrument: pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bandstand on wheels, to go to the audience. It is at the kites.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Till's Teas will sponsor the motorway lamps, in tea colour. Milky.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose by our ten-thousandth coach. Lean on the hedge, as we do.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An arcade sign: PRIZE PUMPKIN, THIS WAY. It points outside.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Lend us the spotters' footbridge. Coaches are a loyal audience: they keep coming.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Light the lay-by for night spotting. The marrows may not sleep.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Kites get the harbour wall. Anglers may apply to sit on the water.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Cushion the harbour wall, for the echo. Then the bandstand. Then the band.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A kite that lands in a hedge now belongs to it. Form attached.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Hear the harbour band by telephone, for the camera. Nod.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A lake lighthouse, for floats at dusk. It goes in the marrow bed.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Lamp-post signs: KITES MAY REST HERE. In place of SHOPS THIS WAY.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Trim the arcade hedge. Then the awnings, to match. Then the hats.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Dim the Guild's harbour windows at dusk. The water is 40 % hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The band will hire a lighthouse to play from. One bar per step, up to the top.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Unhook the telephones for the Quiet Competition. Till's Teas is ringing.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will pay to keep the bandstand in trim. Shears are packed.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Walk the arcade with the band, carrying cymbals. Carrying only.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A landing circle by the marrows. Kites miss circles by 3 metres.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay to put the pumpkin on the motorway signs. Coaches may follow it.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Launch a kite named after you. Smile before it finds the hedge.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay for dark harbour lamps at concerts. The band knows 30 % by heart.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A study: is a coach late if nobody waits for it? The Guild is asked to wait.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lateness study asks the Guild to wait at every stop, in turn.

papers.text: Your face on the National Clock. At noon both hands point at you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study of marrows by lamplight. Half the high street goes dark, as a control.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study now needs the lit half dark, and the dark half lit.

papers.text: A desk lamp. It glows near ribbons. Any openings soon? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the lamp: it would like a solo at the Sunday concert.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S LAMP GIVEN SOLO; BAND PLAYS IN THE DARK
clippings.refuse: LAMP STAYS ON THE DESK, GLOWING AT NOTHING

papers.text: Light up the hedge show for the camera. Kites stay down until you smile.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A study on the lighthouse window display. Shortlist: LIGHT, LIGHTHOUSE.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lighthouse study now wishes to dress the beam. In stripes.

papers.text: Flash your initials from a lighthouse. Then your name, all night.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is a humming kite an instrument? If so, it joins the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite study asks to hear a whistling kite, and one that sighs.

papers.text: A plaque on each lamp: LIT BY THE PRESIDENT. I have done four.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Does the anglers' willow need permission to droop? A study.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The willow study asks to inspect every willow for drooping.

papers.text: Three small umbrellas, one per telephone. Bad lines are so damp.
papers.subject: vanity

favour.text: About the umbrellas: they wish to judge the marrow show. Open.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S UMBRELLA JUDGES MARROWS; GROWERS DAMP
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLAS STAY BY THE TELEPHONES, OPINIONS UNSHARED

papers.text: Kites land on awnings. A study finds 9 in 10 prefer stripes.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning study asks to try plain awnings too. And spots.
